title: EOL Tracker normalized software record (not OpenEoX Core)

research.description: One-time researched provenance (AGENTS.md rule 8 tier b). Present only on records a human or agent contributed for a product no deterministic source covers; absent on every record an importer owns. The quote is the vendor sentence, stored verbatim with normalized whitespace, that states the dates beside it.

verified_at.description: When the quote was last confirmed against source_url. null means the evidence was admitted from store only and has never been refetched.

stale_after.description: Explicit review deadline, when the contributor set one. Null falls back to the 180-day freshness horizon on the record's last_checked.

derived_entry.description: One derived milestone's provenance, keyed by the milestone it explains under `milestone_provenance`. A derived date is arithmetic on a base date and a rule the vendor states explicitly — a duration, the release that ends this one, or the parent platform whose lifecycle this component follows — so the base, the rule and the page it was read from are all published beside the result, and `engine/derived.py` re-derives the result from them. There is deliberately no `result` field: the result is the milestone value this entry sits beside, which is what makes a tampered date detectable (it stops matching its own rule). The derived value keeps the width its evidence states: a month-only trigger or parent date yields a `YYYY-MM` milestone (see AGENTS.md rule 4), and `base_date` stays a full ISO day because the arithmetic starts from a stated day.

kind.description: Always `derived`, so a computed date can never be read as a vendor statement.

method.description: The published rule shape. `release-plus-duration`: the vendor states a duration from a stated base date. `release-trigger`: the vendor states which release ends this one. `support-inheritance`: the vendor states that this component follows its parent platform's lifecycle.

source_url.description: The page the rule and the base date were read from.

quote.description: The vendor sentence that states the rule, verbatim with normalized whitespace. This is the evidence that licenses the derivation.

base_date.description: The stated date the rule starts from, as a full ISO day: the release's own milestone, or the parent's stated deadline. Never a date this entry invents.

base_label.description: What the base date is, in the source's own terms — for example `general availability`, or the parent row's label.

duration.description: Present only for `release-plus-duration`. A positive whole number of calendar days, months or years from `base_date`. Months and years are calendar arithmetic, so a result that would land past the end of its month clamps to that month's last day. Cadence is not a duration: an approximate release interval is not representable here.

trigger.description: Present only for `release-trigger`. The release whose own publication ends this one's support; its `date` is that release's published date and IS the derived deadline, at the width the source states — an ISO day, or `YYYY-MM` when the source names only a month. It must match the milestone's precision exactly.

parent.description: Present only for `support-inheritance`. The published parent whose lifecycle this record's dates follow. `milestone` names which of the parent's normalized milestones is inherited (an end milestone, never general availability) and `date` is that milestone's date, which IS the derived deadline, at the width the parent states — an ISO day, or `YYYY-MM`. It must match this milestone's precision exactly.

milestone_provenance.description: Optional, release-level, keyed by the milestone names this release derives rather than states. Only a non-null milestone may appear: an absent date stays absent, and a rule alone would fill it. A record whose dates are all vendor-stated carries no such key, so every existing record validates unchanged.

evidence.description: One stored verbatim quote and the page it came from. Every milestone the record states must appear, at the same day precision, in a quote that backs it.

ga.description: Calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) or month precision (YYYY-MM) when the source publishes no day. A month is never padded to a day.

verifier.description: The pipeline that owns this record: the deterministic importer's fixed id (deterministic-<source-slug>; the registry in engine/sources.py decides which ones exist and which catalog each owns), or researched-<contributor-slug> for a one-time researched contribution. The pattern admits a new collector; only a registered source is published.
